etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English apart, aparte, a-part, a part, from Anglo-Norman a part, from Latin ad partem (“to the side”).

definitions.definition: Placed separately (in regard to space or time).

quote.citation: 2015, Johnny Rogan, Ray Davies: A Complicated Life:
quote.text: We had a large bus and I had two of them at the front and two at the back, and I had to sit in the middle and keep them apart.
Others apart sat on a hill retired.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Psalms 4:3:
quote.text: But know that the Lord hath set apart him that is godly for himself.

definitions.definition: In or into two or more parts.

quote.citation: 1980, Joy Division (lyrics and music), “Love Will Tear Us Apart”:
quote.text: Love, love will tear us apart, again.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, James 1:21:
quote.text: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.

quote.citation: 1827, John Keble, “The Snow-Drop”, in The Christian Year:
quote.text: Let Pleasure go, put Care apart.

definitions.definition: (used following a noun) Excluded from consideration.
(after a noun or in the predicate) Exceptional, distinct.
Having been taken apart; disassembled, in pieces.

quote.citation: 1838 (date written), L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter XIV, in Lady Anne Granard; or, Keeping up Appearances. […], volume I, London: Henry Colburn, […], published 1842, →OCLC, page 172:
quote.text: The young lover was in waiting, to hand them out of the large substantial carriage, and the first quiet moment that he could find for an apart whisper, said, "What can be the reason that your mother has never taken the slightest notice of my letter?"

quote.citation: 2016, Jasmine Railey, Carter and Ayanna 2: A Hood Love‎[1] (Fiction), →ISBN, →OCLC, page 231:
quote.text: I killed a man. This was never apart[sic – meaning a part] of the plan, Tracy was supposed to do all of the dirty work.
